entries.english_draft:
{center}*** Ten Tips for Adventurers ***

{center}By the King

1. You and the monsters take turns. Do not rush!

2. Checking your items or changing direction does not use up a turn.

3. When fleeing, watch out for enemies attacking diagonally!

4. Walking restores HP. When danger threatens, run away first!

5. Check if monsters are awake or asleep. You needn't defeat them all!

6. Drink a Zoom herb if trapped! Throw Misleader herbs at monsters!

7. At full HP, drinking a Medicinal herb or Super herb raises max HP a little.

8. A Lightning staff never misses! A Bazoom staff sends enemies away!

9. A Fuddle staff confuses your foe. A Snooze staff puts your foe to sleep!

10. Use an Antidotal herb to restore strength lost to poison.

Only then drink a Seed of strength!

{center}That is all.

entries.english_draft:
Old man: Warriors learn skills!

Old man: Set those skills on swords and shields to use them.

Old man: You can set up to three skills on each sword or shield, but some combinations are incompatible.

Old man: Skills you cannot set have red names.

Old man: Once set, a skill cannot be removed until you leave the dungeon.

Old man: Using skills makes you hungry. The stronger the skill, the more hunger it costs. Choose your moment wisely.

Old man: Swords and shields with skills set on them can be broken by traps or critical hits.

Old man: One more warning...

Old man: Warriors cannot use scrolls, staves or rings.

Old man: Remember that.

Trick-loving youth: If you swap places, it's a Tradespot staff.

Trick-loving youth: If the monster turns into a priest, it's definitely a Decoy staff!

Trick-loving youth: See? You can work out quite a few staves that way without using a Peep scroll.

Trick-loving youth: But be careful!

Trick-loving youth: Try it on a weak monster from far away, or you could be in trouble.

entries.english_draft:
Listen, everyone!

Guess what! Our very own water jar is engaged!

Eee! Congratulations!

And who's the lucky lady? Apparently, it's Milun!

She's a little older, but I think they make a lovely couple!

Still, is it really all right to leave Pamela in the lurch...?

...Oops! That was supposed to be a secret.

Silly Remi! Hee hee!{heart}

It's my little secret!

I'd love to write about it, but that wouldn't be fair to the water jar.

I'll have to settle for writing it in my diary.

entries.japanese:
{unclassified-control:14}レミィの日記⑮

　・・・コラっ！
　アンタ　ﾅﾆ読ﾝでﾝﾉﾖっ！
　ﾋﾄﾉ日記を　読ﾑﾅﾝﾃサイテー！
　ｿﾝﾅ人ﾊ　バシルーラﾖっ！
　・・・っﾃ書ｲﾄｹば
　ﾐﾝﾅ　ｺﾜがっﾃ読ﾏﾅｲｶﾓﾈ。
　レミィっﾃ　アッタマｲｲ～　ｳﾌ⑮

　ｻﾃﾄ・・・。

　ｷょｳﾊ　ｱﾉ水ガメｸﾝが
　コンヤクｼﾀｺﾄを　教ｴﾃｸﾚﾀﾉ。
　ｵ相手ﾊ　ﾅﾝﾄミルンｻﾝ！

　水ガメｸﾝっﾃ　ｱｱ見ｴﾃﾓ
　ｹっｺｳ年増好ﾐﾅﾉﾈぇ～。
　ﾁょっﾄビックリ！

　ｿﾚﾆｼﾃﾓ　ｵﾅじ水ガメﾉ
　パメラﾁゃﾝﾉｺﾄﾊ
　どｳｽﾙﾂﾓﾘﾅﾉｶｼﾗﾈ～。
　カノジョ　ｿﾉ気だっﾀﾉﾆ・・・。
　ｷっﾄ　今でﾓ
　ガイバーラｻﾝﾉｵ店ﾉ前で
　水ガメｸﾝﾉｺﾄ
　ﾏっﾃﾙﾝだﾛｳﾅぁ～。
　ﾁょっﾄｶﾜｲｿｳ・・・。
entries.english_draft:
{center}Remi's diary{heart}

...Hey! What do you think you're reading?!

Reading someone else's diary is awful!

I'll Bazoom anyone who does it!

...There. Maybe writing that will scare people off.

Remi, you're so clever! Hee hee!{heart}

Now then...

Today, the water jar told me he's engaged.

And the lucky lady is Milun!

Who'd have thought he had such a taste for older women? What a surprise!

But what does he plan to do about Pamela, the other water jar?

She was so keen on him...

I bet she's still outside Gaibara's shop, waiting for him.

Poor thing...

{center}showed the marriage registration!

Milun: ...Oh, right. Could you tell the armour something for me?

Milun: I'd be delighted to accept his invitation to go on a date.

entries.english_draft:
{center}The shield spoke softly.

Shield: Oh, my. What a surprise. It seems you can hear my voice.

Shield: Look at this scar.

Shield: I received it while protecting Giga from a blow of the dragon's claws.

Shield: Whenever I see it, I cannot help remembering his gentle smile.

Shield: And yet, those people... As soon as the dragon was gone, they began calling Giga a monster.

Shield: It is true that he was very large for a human.

Shield: But to treat their hero as a monster for that alone...

Shield: I-I'm sorry. The tears are coming again...

Shield: Please ask the armour over there for the rest.

entries.english_draft:
{center}The armour was murmuring sadly.

Armour: ...Humans are such weak creatures, aren't they?

Armour: They say they want peace, but they can't even come together without a villain to oppose.

Armour: That would be bad enough...

Armour: But when there isn't a villain, they force someone into the role.

Armour: Then they compare themselves to that person and decide they're good people.

Armour: ...Sound familiar?

Armour: Humans would probably get angry and say it isn't true. But that's how it looks to me.

Armour: ...Oh, sorry. I apologise if I've upset you.

Armour: The truth is... Something's been troubling me.

Armour: Sorry. That's why I let those harsh words slip out.

Armour: Ask the old helmet over there for the rest.

entries.english_draft:
{center}{player} peered into the jar.

A memory of distant days appears on the water's surface.

An old man slowly descends a mountain.

His face is deeply lined. His eyes gaze into the distance.

He might be any old man, but for his body. He is enormous.

He no longer has the strength he once did. Nor does he carry the sword and shield he used against the dragon.

At the foot of the mountain, the old man walks towards a small village.

On its outskirts lies an ancient underground cemetery.

He quietly descends its stairs, step by step, as though savouring each one.

The villagers watch him go. They speak to one another in whispers.

'That's the man who defeated the dragon...'

'He's come down from the mountain.'

'But why the cemetery?'

'Surely... He hasn't gone there to die?'

The old giant never returned to the surface.

Flowers blooming near the cemetery swayed in the fresh breeze.

Flower: If all humans were like you, I'd put even more effort into blooming beautifully.

Flower: ...Hee hee.

Flower: See you again.

entries.english_draft:
{center}The note continues the fish's tale.

Goldfish: Somehow, I ended up staying in Ethiopia for three years.

Goldfish: I even went out with the turtle for a while.

Goldfish: But I never forgot Toshi...

Goldfish: The turtle had a shell, but Toshi was my shell-mate.

Goldfish: Oh, not funny? Sorry. I'm no good at jokes.

Goldfish: What? Why did I leave Ethiopia?

Goldfish: The worms didn't agree with me.

Goldfish: And however much time passed, I couldn't forget Toshi.

Goldfish: One day, I said goodbye to the turtle and boarded a cargo ship.

Goldfish: He was timid, but he was a good sort.

Goldfish: We even threw farewell streamers.

Goldfish: The turtle cried at the end. And I... Wait a minute.

Goldfish: Come to think of it, why did he take me to Ethiopia?

Goldfish: I never asked him.

Goldfish: Oh, well... That's the end of my story.

Goldfish: Thanks for listening to me ramble on.

Goldfish: Look in the water jar outside this shop. I've a thank-you gift for you.

entries.english_draft:
Toshi: I found out afterwards... Just as the octopus squirted his ink, a whale was swimming slowly past.

Toshi: Yoko says she waited for the ink to clear, but she was looking at the whale's dark body.

Toshi: And the ship's whistle she heard? That was the whale spouting!

Toshi: She's a bit of a dreamer. Can't be helped!

Toshi: Anyway, the whale swallowed me and the octopus.

Toshi: I must've been in there for about three years. Even became friends with the octopus.

Toshi: One day, the whale swallowed a strange scroll.

Toshi: I read it, and somehow I ended up in this water jar.

Toshi: Apparently, it takes you home. An Evac scroll, they call it. Remi told me.

Toshi: Don't ask me why, but I suppose that makes this jar my home.

Toshi: We're happy now. Wonder if the octopus is still inside that whale...

Toshi: Thanks for listening. See you!
